title: Hippocampal sequences represent working memory and implicit timing
goal: Surpass the source-paper result on the same task: Original time decoding predicts one of seven elapsed-time bins during the short-delay window, separately for standard-short and standard-long cues. Retain the original behavior, sequence and odor analyses as required context, without turning their biological contrast into a decoder score.
primary_outputs: Candidate method and outputs for the source task: Original time decoding predicts one of seven elapsed-time bins during the short-delay window, separately for standard-short and standard-long cues. Retain the original behavior, sequence and odor analyses as required context, without turning their biological contrast into a decoder score.

Source-paper comparison for Fig. 4D Pearson time-bin decoding correlation, preserving standard-short and standard-long panels: Pearson correlation corr(allrealbin,allpredbin), not fraction-correct accuracy, measures predicted versus actual bin indices across held-out trials. Higher correlation is the ordered decoder direction.
success_criteria: Authenticate the published per-session time-decoding results and independently rerun the original native baseline on the complete 11-animal, 44-session cohort.
Use original seven-bin labels, standard-trial membership, full-trial leave-one-out support, eligibility, source processed inputs and correlation aggregation for both methods.
Predeclare a meaningful gain and valid animal-level uncertainty without selecting favorable cues, days or mice; retain all original output families as contextual controls.
Changing to the no-smoothing/no-flooring input, a prospective split or combined score defines an extension and cannot establish the original paper win.
The bound improvement contract must be improvement_ready and its complete same-task comparison and admission requirements must pass.
Reproduction is calibration only; reconstructing a numerical result, changing the task or split, or achieving stronger significance alone is not success.
